concept.title: Connect to a Git Server
concept.shortdesc: The Git Client connects to GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and other servers over HTTPS or SSH, and remembers your credentials per server.

conbody.p: When you push, pull, fetch, or clone from a private repository, the server asks for credentials. The Git Client supports two connection types:

ul.li: HTTPS - You authenticate with a username and a personal access token (or a password, where the server still allows it).
SSH - You authenticate with an SSH key, optionally through an SSH agent.

conbody.p: The Git Client stores one set of credentials per server, encrypted in the options. If no credentials are stored, it prompts you the first time they are needed. To change accounts or clear stored credentials, see .
